form_002:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the data needed to pre-fill the IRS EIN application (Form SS-4) for my newly incorporated company. This is a preparation step only — you will not submit anything to the IRS.

If you don't already have them, ask me for the following details before proceeding:
- Legal name of the entity exactly as filed with the state
- Entity type (LLC, C-corp, S-corp, partnership, etc.)
- State and date of incorporation
- Principal business address and mailing address (if different)
- Responsible party's full legal name and SSN/ITIN (do not ask me to paste this into any file you generate — just confirm you have it and will insert it directly on the form when we get there)
- County and state where the business is physically located
- Reason for applying (started new business, hired employees, banking purposes, etc.)
- Principal business activity and a brief description of products/services
- Expected number of employees in the next 12 months, and first date wages will be paid (if applicable)
- Closing month of accounting year

Use your configured credentials to pull any of this company information from our incorporation records, document storage, or company database if such access is available, so you minimize what you need to ask me directly.

Once collected, organize all fields into a clear, labeled checklist formatted to match the sections of Form SS-4, so it can be quickly copied into the IRS online EIN application or a paper form later. Flag any fields that are missing, ambiguous, or need my confirmation (especially the responsible party's identity and the reason for applying, since these affect IRS processing).

When done, report back: (1) the completed pre-fill checklist, (2) any fields still missing or needing my input, and (3) a note that actually submitting the application remains a human step.

form_002:n3.prompt:
You are helping me get an Employer Identification Number (EIN) for my newly incorporated company by preparing the online EIN application through {{vendor}}. Federal rules require the company's responsible party to personally complete and certify this application under penalty of perjury, so you prepare everything, then stop for human sign-off. Do not certify, sign, accept terms, or submit on my behalf.

First, ask me for anything missing:
- Legal company name exactly as on the formation documents, entity type, and state and date of incorporation
- Responsible party's full legal name and title (I will enter their tax ID number myself)
- Business mailing and physical address, county, and phone
- Principal activity, reason for applying (e.g., started a new business), and fiscal year end
- Expected employees in the next 12 months and first wage date, if any

Then:
1. Use {{vendor}}'s published pages to confirm what stands between me and filing: account, identity-proofing, or credential requirements; operating hours; session timeouts; and any per-day limits. Use your configured credentials only if {{vendor}} requires them for read-only research.
2. Find the official EIN application form and its instructions, downloadable without an account, and note the paper, fax, or mail fallback with the exact addresses, numbers, and forms {{vendor}} publishes, in case the online flow is unavailable.
3. Build a field-by-field worksheet that maps my answers to each question in the online flow, in order, and flag any answer that is ambiguous.

Done looks like this: a completed worksheet, a short summary of eligibility, hours, and timeout limits, and the fallback filing details. Report these back to me, then stop for human sign-off so the responsible party can enter the sensitive data, certify, and submit the application personally.

form_002:n4.prompt:
You are helping me store our company's newly issued EIN securely in our official company records after we've completed the IRS EIN application. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: the EIN itself (or confirm it's already saved somewhere you can access, like a downloaded IRS confirmation letter/CP 575 notice), the legal company name and formation date as they appear on the EIN confirmation, and where I want the record stored (e.g., a specific folder in Google Drive, Dropbox, a password manager's secure notes, or a company records app I use).

2. If I have the IRS confirmation document (PDF or scan), help me file it in the designated location with a clear, consistent filename such as "[CompanyName]_EIN_Confirmation_[Year].pdf".

3. Create or update a company records entry (e.g., in a shared document, spreadsheet, or records tool I specify) that logs: the EIN, the exact legal entity name, date of issuance, and the storage location/link of the confirmation document. Do not write the EIN into chat logs, code, or any insecure or public location—use your configured credentials to access whatever secure storage tool I designate.

4. Double-check the EIN format (9 digits, XX-XXXXXXX) and that the legal name matches our incorporation documents exactly; flag any mismatch to me.

5. Confirm the record is saved and accessible, and note who else (e.g., accountant, co-founders) may need access, asking me if you should share the location with them.

When done, report back: where the EIN and confirmation document are now stored, the exact record format used, and any discrepancies or missing information you found. If any part of this requires me to review or approve access permissions before sharing, stop for human sign-off before proceeding further.
